text:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager alert: 3xx/5xx spike in eu-west-3 for inference-hosting service. Symptoms: DNS lookups timing out for multiple AZs, elevated client 502s. Pager: #oncall-az-network

alice: i'm seeing the same in grafana, added dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/r/xyz. quick check: NAT egress errors spike, and route propagation metrics show delay for rt-azb (route table).

ben: paging neteng/infra — could be route table tag drift after last terraform apply. @carol can you confirm recent infra deploys?

carol: I rolled a route-tagging change in eu-west-3 ~40m ago to standardize route table naming. Applied via terraform run: `tf apply -target=aws_route_table_association.rta-eu-west-3` then a followup plan removed and re-created an assoc for private subnet az-b. I saw one assoc failure but terraform completed with retries.

frank: checking VPC flow logs, I see asymmetric return paths for instances in az-b subnet-12. Some flows show src nat-gw-a (in az-a) for traffic from az-b — looks like route assoc switched to the wrong NAT gateway in the same region.

alice: customer impact: multiple customers reporting brief 502s and timeouts for embeddings + small inference calls. severity: P2 escalating to P1 if widespread. Metrics: error-rate went from 0.3% to 7% across eu-west-3.

incident-bot: @oncall-rotation triggered. Handoff initiated: alice -> ben. Next oncall: carol in 30m.

ben: short-term mitigation — let's pin affected subnets to NAT in the same AZ. I can run a targeted re-assoc to the correct nat-gw-b for az-b private subnets. Anyone opposed?

eve: +1 do it. also let's prepare fallback: add a route to force egress via internet gateway for healthcheck traffic so control-plane calls pass.

carol: i'm attaching the quick commands i'm going to run from console (console-first to avoid terraform state drift):
```
# list associations
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=tag:Name,Values=rt-az-b*" --region eu-west-3
# associate correct nat
aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id rtb-0abcd1234 --subnet-id subnet-0b1234 --region eu-west-3
# verify nat gw
aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter "Name=subnet-id,Values=subnet-0b1234" --region eu-west-3
```

frank: before re-assoc, capture current conntrack counts on NAT instances/gateways and dump netstat on a couple of affected hosts — we want to avoid breaking existing conntracking (some connections are mid-flight).

alice: frank, can you collect conntrack and share snippet?

frank: pasted sample from host-azb-01: `conntrack -S` shows conntrack table near capacity 78%. NAT gateway metrics show ephemeral TCP translation errors increasing.

ben: ok i'm comfortable with targeted re-assoc. carol, when you associate, please do one subnet at a time and wait 60s to observe. We'll have deploy-bot hold any AG deployment in eu-west-3.

deploy-bot: HOLD placed on ag-deploy eu-west-3 for 60m by ben.

carol: starting assoc for subnet-0b1234 -> rtb-0abcd1234 (expected nat-gw-b). Doing manual assoc now.

ops-bot: audit: terraform workspace=prod, user=carol, action=route-table-association, region=eu-west-3, resource=subnet-0b1234

carol: assoc complete. verifying... traceroute to 8.8.8.8 from app-host-azb shows next hop nat-gw-b.

alice: metrics stabilizing — 5xx rate down to 2.1%. DNS lookup latency still elevated for a subset of customers.

frank: I still see some DNS query timeouts from the az-b resolver (172.31.0.2). Flushing local dns cache on a few nodes seems to help. Suggest we rotate the Route53 resolver endpoints in that VPC to refresh.

ben: agree. carol, can you update dhcp options / resolvers to force restart? We should avoid creating more change noise.

carol: I'll trigger a controlled restart of the dnsmasq process on the affected bastion pool and kick the clients via SSM `sudo systemctl restart dnsmasq`. Doing in waves of 10 hosts.

alice: customer reported heavy 502s at 09:12 UTC — we started mitigation at ~09:38 UTC. I'll draft status note: partial outage impacting inference requests for EU region, mitigations in progress.

incident-bot: Reminder: create incident-report doc in /incidents/postmortems and capture timeline.

ben: after assoc and dns restart, error rate dropped to 0.6% and latency back to baseline within 10m. Moving to recovery phase. Removing deploy hold.

deploy-bot: HOLD cleared on ag-deploy eu-west-3 by ben.

carol: followup actions: 1) reconcile terraform state to reflect manual assoc (run `terraform import aws_route_table_association.rta-azb rta-xxxxx`), 2) add automated guard in infra pipeline to validate route-table tags won't be removed during rename, 3) add route propagation alert for route-table assoc drift.

frank: also recommend a runbook step: on nat assoc failure, verify conntrack utilization and perform per-subnet reassoc instead of blanket re-assoc.

alice: i'll open the incident doc and add customer-impact snippets + slack timeline. can someone volunteer to own postmortem? @frank?

frank: i'll own the postmortem. will include timeline, terraform mitigation, and guardrails.

prs: @pagerduty: update on-call schedule to reflect handoff notes.

incident-bot: Incident closed for paging at 10:48 UTC. Please complete postmortem within 72h. :white_check_mark:

alice: thanks everyone. postmortem to include specific terraform diffs, a script to re-associate correctly, and ATDD for route tag changes.

ben: one more note — we should add a canary subnet test that performs an e2e DNS + egress check post-terraform change to catch this before rollout.

carol: agreed. I'll add the canary to the infra backlog.

alice: closing channel thread, moving followups to #eng-infra and /incidents/postmortems/3967890123-route-tag-dns-translation-surge.md
